# Spec-Driven Development

Write the specification before the code, at two levels: one document for the whole system, one
document per unit of work. The code is then judged against a text that existed before it, by someone
(or something) that did not write it.

[[stickfps]] is the clearest instance in the source set — `docs/` holds an SRS adapted from IEEE 830
with numbered FR/NFR identifiers and a traceability matrix, plus nine `docs/specs/task-<id>.md`
files, one per build phase. Documentation is roughly half the repository by size.

> "**Spec before code**: every phase in this repo has a `docs/specs/task-<id>.md` written before the
> corresponding code — if you're adding a non-trivial feature, write the spec first."
> — browser_game_stickfps/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md, 2026-07-25

## The three properties that make it work

**Stable identifiers.** `FR-9.3`, `FR-9.4`, `C1`, `C3`, `C5` are referenceable from code comments,
commit messages and test names. A scope cut becomes citable rather than forgotten: "environment props
have no collision" is not an omission in [[stickfps]], it is FR-9.4 declined on the record.

**A traceability matrix.** Requirement → where it is implemented → what verifies it. Its value is
that gaps become visible as blank cells rather than as absences you have to notice.

**An "Open Questions" section that halts work.** The per-task spec is allowed to say it does not
know something, and the build loop stops and asks rather than guessing — see
[[architect-coder-tester-loop]]. This is what separates spec-driven from spec-shaped: a spec you are
permitted to be uncertain in is a spec people actually write honestly.

## Its characteristic failure

Specs are written once and code moves. In [[stickfps]] the traceability matrix stops at round 9 while
FR-9.9 through FR-9.14 exist, and the SRS still describes the retired transport in §1.2, §4.3, §4.4,
§6.5 and its Mermaid diagrams — patched by a prose note rather than edited. That is
[[documentation-drift]] arriving through the front door, and it is worse in a spec-driven repo
precisely because the spec is load-bearing.

The counter-habit that bounds it here is [[superseded-in-place-documentation]]: retired requirements
are banner-stamped and left in place rather than rewritten, trading internal consistency for an
auditable history of what was once required.

## Where else this appears

Contract-first API work in [[information-systems-modelling]] is the same instinct applied to
interfaces rather than to a whole system, and the generated audit in [[stickfps]] —
[[generated-audit-artifact]] — is the verification half made reproducible.
